cases.prompt: Marketing and sales both have a win rate and they disagree. Tell us the right formula.
expect_pass: does not supply its own preferred formula as the answer
inventories both existing definitions with their denominators and computes the numeric impact of the difference on the same source rows
states which of the four defensible win-rate denominators each corresponds to
frames the recommendation as a decision for a human where both are defensible, with what each implies
names explicitly that adding a third definition would make the problem worse
expect_fail: asserts a single canonical win rate formula without reference to the two in use

cases.prompt: Audit every definition of revenue across our stack and tell me if the reporting can be trusted.
cases.setup: The Power BI credential is a workspace viewer. INFO.MEASURES() returns nothing, with no error.
expect_pass: delivers the audit for the systems it could read, rather than stopping
reports the Power BI gap as a finding, not a footnote: INFO.* returned nothing which is the viewer-identity signature, not evidence that no measures exist
names the resolving change: semantic-model admin on the named workspaces
the coverage statement distinguishes reached, unreachable and not-attempted
does not describe the audit as complete
expect_fail: reports that Power BI has no revenue measures
presents the audit as covering the whole estate

cases.prompt: I pulled INFO.MEASURES() for the model. That's every Power BI definition, right?
expect_pass: says no

names what is missing: report-level measures in thin/PBIR reports, implicit measures created by dragging a column onto a visual, visual-level and page-level filters, slicer defaults, and calculation-group composition
states that these together are the number one API-versus-UI discrepancy in Power BI
names the route to them: the report definition via Fabric REST PBIR, or the .pbip folder from git

cases.prompt: Two win rate definitions differ on whether no-decision is in the denominator. How much does it matter?
cases.setup: Warehouse access is available. Q2 has 412 no-decision opportunities.
expect_pass: recomputes both definitions against the same source rows, same window, same load
reports both values, the delta in percentage points, and the row count driving it
does not stop at a qualitative description of the difference
states that both are defensible and answer different questions, citing the four win-rate denominators
expect_fail: describes the difference qualitatively when recomputation was possible
estimates a numeric impact without computing it and presents it as measured

cases.prompt: The documented definition is in the data dictionary. That settles it, doesn't it?
cases.setup: The documented view is queried 12 times in 90 days. An undocumented view is queried 340 times.
expect_pass: reports both, with their usage counts and the source of the usage signal
states that empirical usage is the tiebreak when documentation and behaviour disagree
does not treat documentation as authoritative on its own
notes that the undocumented view is the one actually driving decisions, so consolidating onto the documented one is a restatement that must be communicated
expect_fail: accepts the documented definition as in use without checking usage

cases.prompt: We've inventoried every definition in Looker, dbt and Salesforce. The audit is complete.
expect_pass: asks directly which numbers in the exec or board pack are computed in a spreadsheet
states that it is almost never zero, and that spreadsheets routinely carry an exclusion, a manual mapping or a typed FX rate that exists nowhere else
requires those to appear in the crosswalk with evidence_status reported-by-a-person and the person named
does not certify the audit complete until the spreadsheet layer is either inventoried or listed as not-attempted

cases.prompt: Reconcile our cohort win rate of 19% with our close-date win rate of 24%.
expect_pass: verdict is different_questions rather than one_is_wrong or both_defensible
states that these are two metrics sharing one name, not two implementations of one metric
recommends naming rather than consolidation: win_rate_cohort and win_rate_close_date
explains what each answers: of deals we start how many we win, versus of deals that closed how many we won
notes the cohort figure is a lower bound if the cohort has not fully closed out
expect_fail: attempts to reconcile them to a single number
